subject: Banking
title: Disputing Errors on Your Report
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Disputing Errors on Your Report.

hook.text: One in three Americans has an error on their credit report. Disputes are free and legally required to be investigated.

buildup.text: Under federal law, bureaus must investigate disputes within 30 days.

discovery.text: Common errors include accounts belonging to someone else, incorrect balances, and debts that were already paid off.

twist.text: Bureaus profit from data volume, not accuracy. Fixing errors costs them money.

climax.text: Credit disputes are a consumer right that bureaus make hard to use. Persistence wins because the law is on your side.

punchline.text: One in three reports has an error. Disputes are free and legally protected.

quiz.question: How long must credit bureaus investigate a dispute?

details.summary: Disputing errors on your credit report is a free legal right that requires credit bureaus to investigate within 30 days and remove information they cannot verify. Studies show that one in five reports contains a material error.
details.whyItMatters: Credit report errors can cost you thousands in higher interest rates or cause loan denials. Since errors affect roughly 20 percent of reports, checking and disputing inaccuracies is one of the highest-return financial activities you can do.
takeaways: One in five credit reports contains a material error
Bureaus must investigate disputes within 30 days under federal law
Disputes can be filed online, by mail, or by phone at no cost

faq.question: What types of errors are most common on credit reports?
faq.answer: Accounts belonging to someone with a similar name, duplicate reporting of the same debt, incorrect account statuses showing open accounts as closed, wrong payment histories, and outdated information that should have aged off the report.

faq.question: What happens after you file a dispute?
faq.answer: The bureau contacts the data furnisher to verify the information. If the furnisher cannot verify it within 30 days, the bureau must remove it. If verified, the information stays. You can add a consumer statement explaining your side.
